solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Agent holding boy is about to nod off

indicators.note: the agent's word holds the boy's name inside it

parts.note: an agent here is a secret agent, a spy

explanation.surface: A spy with a lad in custody is starting to drift off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy is drowsy and close to falling asleep, which is what being about to nod off means.

clue.text: Showing injury, frightened about start of raid

indicators.note: the frightened word goes about, around, the letter taken from raid
start of takes only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Wounded and terrified after the opening of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred means marked by healed wounds, so it shows signs of past injury.

clue.text: Include revised cops' names

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Add in the police officers' names after the list was updated.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass something is to take it in or embrace it within a wider whole, so to include it.

clue.text: French lad with clothes taken from French revolutionary

indicators.note: the word for clothes is removed from the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Robespierre was a leader of the French Revolution's Reign of Terror

explanation.surface: A French boy has his garments stripped by a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre is a common French boy's first name, the French form of Peter.

clue.text: Dukes flanking English girl, as stated

indicators.note: the two dukes stand either side of the English girl, so her letters go between them

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Two noblemen on either side of an English lass, as the record says.
explanation.definitionFit: Something declared has been announced or put on record, a synonym of stated in its adjectival sense.

clue.text: Sentamu's old signature on dress lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: An archbishop's former autograph appears on a frock held up.
explanation.walkthrough: John Sentamu was Archbishop of York until 2020, and Archbishops of York sign themselves with the Latin abbreviation for York.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor, short for Eboracum, the Roman name for York, is the official signature of an Archbishop of York.

clue.text: Coffee half-hourly, not so long ago

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: half-hourly here keeps the back half of the word hourly

explanation.surface: Someone recalls drinking coffee every thirty minutes until recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hourly' reads as one word meaning every thirty minutes; split it into the selector 'half' and the word 'hourly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly means recently, in the later part of a period of time.

clue.text: In more ways than one, they may make a fine spray

definitions.meaning: the setter's warning that both senses of the plural are meant

definitions.text: they may make a fine spray
definitions.meaning: a spray is a bunch of flowers, and these blooms make a lovely one; the perforated nozzle of a watering can also makes a fine spray of water

explanation.walkthrough: A spray is both a small bouquet and a mist of water; the answer names popular flowers and also the sprinkler heads on watering cans.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower makes a fine floral spray, and a rose is also the sprinkler nozzle on a watering can or hose.

clue.text: Sedated, oddly determined

indicators.note: oddly means in an unusual way, so the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Drugged, yet strangely resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead set, as in dead set on something, means firmly resolved or fixed in purpose.

clue.text: Ambridge resident is a royal girl

parts.note: Cher is a girl's name, as of the singer

explanation.surface: Someone from a village turns out to be a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the fictional village of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap about a farming family; R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archer family are the central household of the radio serial set in that fictional village.

clue.text: Against girl, Italian woman

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a young woman who happens to be from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a titled noblewoman of Italy.

clue.text: US state or country girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American state, or the nation in the Caucasus with the same name
second meaning: a girl's first name

explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' looks like it joins two separate options, but both halves are one definition, since the name covers a state and a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a southern American state, a nation in the Caucasus, and a woman's given name.

clue.text: Commented about does around boy

indicators.note: the reversed deer goes around the boy's name
about tells us to turn the deer round, reading it backwards

parts.note: does are female deer, so the word gives deer

explanation.surface: Someone passed comment on female deer gathered around a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as the verb but is the plural of doe; 'about' looks like the RE abbreviation but here it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have remarked is to have said something as a comment or observation.

clue.text: Boy with three points on camera attachments

parts.note: S, E and S are compass points, three of them in a row

explanation.surface: A lad with three sharp spikes fitted to his camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenses are the optical glass pieces that fit onto a camera body to focus light.

clue.text: Awkward pause with Kevin Pietersen initially having to state his opinion boldly

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters are put together in a jumbled way
initially takes the first letter of each of the cricketer's two names

explanation.surface: After an awkward silence, the cricketer has to say his piece forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up is to voice one's views openly and loudly rather than staying quiet.

clue.text: Penny and boy's farm truck

parts.note: D stood for a penny in old British money, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny and her lad own a farm vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a girl's name here, but it is the old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low, sturdy cart without sides, used for hauling heavy loads such as barrels.

clue.text: Support girl by junction, driving

parts.note: a T is a junction shaped like the letter, a T-junction

explanation.surface: Holding up a girl standing beside a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Propellent as an adjective means propelling, pushing something forward, which is what driving means here.

clue.text: Send back crowd actor with crash diet

parts.note: an extra is an actor hired to fill out a crowd scene

indicators.note: a crash diet sounds like a regime, but crash signals the letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor in crowd scenes gets sent home for going on a drastic diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash diet' is a familiar phrase, which hides that crash is the signal to rearrange diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite someone is to hand them back to another country's jurisdiction to face trial.

clue.text: ABs began modifying large cushions used as seats

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; ABs are able seamen or abdominal muscles

explanation.surface: Sailors started altering big floor cushions to sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanbags are large fabric sacks filled with beads that people sit on as informal chairs.

clue.text: Some healthy stallion holding boy is very funny

indicators.note: the hidden run of letters holds the boy's name inside it

parts.note: some of the letters of healthy stallion, a run starting at the end of healthy and stopping partway into stallion

explanation.surface: A fit stallion carrying a lad on its back is a hilarious sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterical in its informal sense means extremely amusing, making people laugh uncontrollably.

clue.text: One held to get on with army

parts.note: a host is a large army, as in heavenly host
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A captive has to grow old alongside soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for a demand being met.

clue.text: Particle from active boy

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of matter coming from an energetic lad.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, a basic particle of matter.

clue.text: Hash can appear in Tommy's!

explanation.surface: Stew turns up in a soldier's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a nickname for a British private soldier; the whole clue also describes the soldier's container that the hash is served in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess tin is a soldier's metal cooking and eating container, in which a hash would be served.

clue.text: Girl who says how she tilts?

indicators.note: says points to the sound of her words, not their spelling

parts.note: she might describe her tilting with 'I lean'

explanation.surface: A girl who explains how she leans over to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a girl's given name, originally Irish.

clue.text: Home Counties boy from France is placid

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, abbreviated SE
René is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: A French lad living in the counties around London is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene describes someone untroubled and peaceful, a close synonym of placid.

clue.text: Hurried, getting caught by Henry's farm

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Rushing, a man is captured by a king called Henry on his land.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one in the Americas for raising cattle.

clue.text: Highly moral folk's word plays about girl

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the plural noun

indicators.note: the puns go around the girl's name

explanation.surface: Strait-laced people make jokes about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritans are people with strict moral or religious principles, often disapproving of pleasure.

clue.text: And another girl who tilts, we're told

indicators.note: we're told points to a word heard, not spelt

parts.note: someone who tilts is a leaner

explanation.surface: A second girl who leans to one side, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the r of leaner is silent, so the word sounds like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lena is a girl's given name, short for names such as Helena.

clue.text: Wayward dean without boy is now tough

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters sit outside the boy's name
a wayward thing goes astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly college dean, once the lad has gone, has hardened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but here it is the old sense of outside, wrapping round the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealed metal or glass has been heated and slowly cooled to make it tougher and less brittle.

clue.text: Take boy to court old widow

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Bring a lad before the judge, says an elderly woman who lost her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an archaic word for a widow, the woman left behind after a husband dies.

clue.text: Wandering sheep with boy, recipient of an NT letter

indicators.note: wandering sheep stray about, so their letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A lad tending stray sheep receives a letter from the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians is a New Testament letter addressed to the Christians of Ephesus.

clue.text: Leading alpinist nurtures boy from the mountains

indicators.note: leading picks the front letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A top mountaineer brings up a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading alpinist' looks like a single expert climber, but the signal takes the first letter of both alpinist and nurtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means belonging to the Andes, the great mountain range of South America.
